Tickers: Netflix (NFLX), Walt Disney (DIS)
Time window: last two fiscal years

kind.description: What the value measures: currency for a money amount, percent for a percentage, multiple for a ratio such as a P/E, count for a number of units such as shares.

unit.description: The unit of value: the ISO 4217 code of a money amount such as USD or DOP, % for a percentage, x for a multiple, the thing counted for a count.

as_of.description: The date the source gives for this figure as YYYY-MM-DD, or null when it gives none.

source_url.description: The URL cited for this figure, or null when no citation was supplied. Figures without a citation are published with a source limitation.

packet.answer_markdown:
**Netflix has been growing revenue far faster than Disney over the last two fiscal years.** Netflix grew roughly 15.7% in FY2024 and about 15.9% in FY2025, while Disney grew roughly 2.8% in FY2024 and about 3.4% in FY2025.

| Company | FY2023 revenue | FY2024 revenue | FY2025 revenue | FY2024 growth | FY2025 growth |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Netflix (fiscal year ends December) | $33.72B | $39.00B | $45.18B | ~15.7% | ~15.9% |
| Walt Disney (fiscal year ends late September) | $88.90B | $91.36B | $94.43B | ~2.8% | ~3.4% |

A few things to keep in mind for a fair comparison:

- Disney is a much larger, more diversified business (parks, film, linear TV, streaming, sports), so its baseline growth tends to be slower than a pure-play streamer like Netflix.
- The two companies are on different fiscal calendars, Netflix's fiscal year matches the calendar year, while Disney's fiscal year ends in late September, so the periods don't line up exactly.
- Netflix's acceleration reflects strength in its subscription business (including paid sharing and ad-tier growth), while Disney's more modest growth reflects mixed results across its traditional media and parks segments alongside expanding streaming.
